content.value: Selection sort repeatedly selects the smallest remaining element and swaps it to the boundary. Insertion sort grows a sorted prefix by shifting larger entries right to make room for the next value. Both preserve the elements but change their order. Trace one pass at a time and distinguish a swap from a shift.

On [4, 2, 3], insertion sort first produces [2, 4, 3], then [2, 3, 4]. Keep key in a temporary variable before shifting. Insertion sort can do little work on already sorted data; selection sort still scans the remaining suffix.
Practice: trace the example by hand, change one input, and explain how the result changes. Check an empty or boundary case when the preconditions allow it.
